Au cœur de la transformation numérique du Crédit Agricole Île-de-France, incarnez un rôle central en tant que Développeur Full-Stack .NET Core, capable de travailler au sein d'une architecture moderne, distribuée et conteneurisée. Imaginez commencer votre journée par un café tout en analysant les derniers services déployés dans le cluster Kubernetes. Le ticketing interne vous présente les nouvelles demandes métiers : chacune nécessite une réflexion technique poussée, une capacité à construire un micro-service propre, robuste, scalable… et parfaitement intégré à l'architecture existante.

Vous échangez ensuite avec les donneurs d'ordre métier pour cadrer précisément les besoins. Votre rôle est essentiel : transformer un besoin fonctionnel en une solution technique pertinente, performante et durable.

✔ Développement de micro-services .NET Core propres, découplés et maintenables.
✔ Intégration dans un environnement Kubernetes / Linux (pods, services, observabilité, bonnes pratiques de résilience).
✔ Manipulation et optimisation de données sous MS SQL.
✔ Interaction avec l'héritage existant PHP, que vous comprenez suffisamment pour y interfacer ou en faire évoluer certaines briques.

Vous êtes force de proposition : vous challengez l'existant, proposez des améliorations, anticipez les impacts d'architecture. Votre pédagogie fait la différence : vous aimez transmettre vos bonnes pratiques aux autres développeurs pour améliorer la qualité globale du code.

En parallèle, la veille technologique est un réflexe naturel : patterns, bonnes pratiques de développement distribués, sécurité, performances… tout ce qui permet de faire évoluer nos services dans le bon sens.

Votre Mission :

  • Concevoir, développer et faire évoluer des micro-services .NET Core dans un environnement cloud-native basé sur Kubernetes, Linux, MS SQL et Git.
  • Interagir avec l'existant PHP lorsque nécessaire, en comprenant les enjeux techniques et les interfaces à maintenir.
  • Piloter vos développements de bout en bout : conception, documentation, qualité du code, tests, intégration et mise en production via des pipelines CI/CD.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes métier pour transformer les besoins en solutions techniques robustes et évolutives.
  • Être force de proposition sur l'architecture applicative : découpage en micro-services, patterns de communication, structuration du code, bonnes pratiques DevOps (sans être un profil infrastructure).
  • Transmettre vos bonnes pratiques de développement moderne (clean code, tests, observabilité, résilience) pour tirer l'équipe vers le haut.

Qui Êtes-Vous ?

Diplômé en informatique, vous affichez une solide expérience en développement back-end et full-stack .NET Core, dans des environnements distribués et orientés micro-services.
Votre maîtrise de .NET Core, des architectures découplées et des pratiques modernes de développement est votre véritable force.

À l'aise dans un écosystème Kubernetes / Linux, vous savez concevoir, déployer et maintenir des services robustes, scalables et observables.
Vous maîtrisez également MS SQL, indispensable pour manipuler et optimiser les données au cœur des processus métiers.

Vous avez déjà travaillé dans des environnements hybrides comprenant un héritage PHP, que vous savez appréhender ou interfacer au besoin - sans que ce soit votre principale spécialité.

Curieux, rigoureux et pédagogue, vous aimez transmettre vos bonnes pratiques de code à l'équipe, challenger l'existant et proposer des améliorations structurantes.
Vous êtes proactif, autonome, tout en appréciant travailler en coopération avec les équipes métier.

Une expérience dans le secteur bancaire est un plus, sans être obligatoire.

Parce que vous rejoignez un environnement où innovation, architecture moderne et excellence technique se rencontrent pour transformer durablement le paysage financier.

Parce que vous prenez un rôle clé dans l'évolution des applications internes d'une grande banque régionale, avec un vrai impact technologique et une vision long terme.

Parce que vous contribuez à des projets d'envergure où vos choix techniques, votre capacité à structurer le code et votre maîtrise des micro-services feront la différence.

About Plane

Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together.

 

Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 55,000+ stars, 5,000+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship.

 

Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules.

 

Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work.

 

Humans and agents

We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's.

 

Most software treats AI as a feature. We treat agents as a kind of worker, and that changes what the system underneath has to be. Agents are only as good as the context they can see and the state they are allowed to change, so shared context, explicit state, durable history, and accountable action are not items on our roadmap. They are the product. Plane is built so that when an agent acts, the humans responsible can see what happened, why, and on whose authority, and the record survives.

 

This is what the infrastructure is for: making the future where humans and agents work together useful, legible, and fully within the organization's control. Every role at Plane is some part of building that.

 

About the role

Our largest customers do not buy Plane off the shelf. A bank wants it behind their firewall with SSO tied to their identity provider; a defense contractor wants it air-gapped with a migration plan from three legacy tools at once. You will own the technical architecture for these deployments before the contract is signed and after, translating what a customer's infrastructure and compliance team requires into a Plane deployment that actually holds up. You will work directly with sales on the largest deals we run and with engineering when a customer's requirements push past what we support today. This role exists because our regulated-industry customers ask questions our sales team cannot answer alone, and our engineers should not have to answer on every call.

 

What you'll do

  • Own the technical architecture for enterprise and regulated-industry deployments, from the first discovery call through a signed statement of work.

  • Design self-hosted and air-gapped Plane deployments that satisfy a specific customer's security review, not a generic best-practice checklist.

  • Run technical discovery with customers whose infrastructure and compliance teams will pick apart every answer you give, and be right often enough that they trust the next one.

  • Define the migration path when a customer moves off two or three existing tools at once, including what data does not survive the move and saying so up front.

  • Work daily with sales on live deals and with engineering when a customer's requirements expose a real gap in the product, carrying that gap back as a specific, scoped request rather than a vague one.

  • Answer the same security questionnaire in a slightly different format for the fourth time this month, because every regulated buyer's procurement process is its own small bureaucracy and none of them read each other's paperwork.

 

What you'll bring

  • You have designed and defended a technical architecture to a skeptical buyer, and you can walk us through one deal where the customer's own security or infrastructure team changed your design.

  • You understand self-hosted and on-premises deployment beyond a docker-compose file, including networking, SSO and identity federation, and what changes when a customer runs the software instead of you.

  • You can read a security questionnaire or compliance requirement and translate it into an actual deployment decision, not a reassurance.

De meeste monteurs in Nederland vervangen vandaag nog steeds ketels die er over tien jaar niet meer staan.

Ben je loodgieter, servicemonteur of cv-monteur? Bij ons stap je over op de techniek die daarvoor in de plaats komt. Ervaring met warmtepompen hoeft niet, die leren we je. Wat je wel meeneemt is je gevoel voor leidingwerk. Geen storingsdienst, een volledig uitgeruste bus, en je werkdag begint als je instapt.

WIJ MAKEN WARMTE ZONDER GAS

Wist je dat wij onze warmtepompen zelf ontwerpen? Met een club van rond de zestig mensen bedenken we ze, assembleren we ze in Utrecht en installeren we ze zelf. Voor huiseigenaren door heel Nederland en sinds dit jaar ook in Duitsland. Vorig jaar won onze Pomp MP als eerste warmtepomp ooit zowel de iF Design Award Gold als de Red Dot.

Elke week gaan er tientallen huizen van het gas af. Het doel is 10% van alle Nederlandse woningen, ongeveer 800.000 huizen. De vraag is er en het product staat. De rem zit op hoe snel we kunnen leveren.

Dat lukt niet zonder jou als servicemonteur.

WAT JIJ HIER DOET

  • Onderhoud aan onze warmtepompen

  • Storingen oplossen die het serviceteam niet op afstand kon verhelpen

  • Installaties inspecteren en optimaliseren

  • Klanten uitleggen wat er aan de hand is, in gewone taal

  • Terugkoppelen wat je in het veld ziet, zodat het product beter wordt

Ongeveer de helft van de storingen zit in onze eigen warmtepomp, waterzijdig of elektrisch. De andere helft zit in de woninginstallatie. Een radiator die niet warm wordt hebben wij niet geplaatst, maar we sturen de klant niet weg. Dat lossen we ook op.

WAAROM MONTEURS BIJ ONS BLIJVEN

Geen storingsdienst. Geen consignatie. Reistijd is werktijd. En jij kiest zelf tussen dertien ADV-dagen of meer salaris per maand.

Ons serviceteam op kantoor lost ongeveer negen van de tien meldingen op afstand op en plant jouw week in. Jij rijdt naar de klanten waar echt iemand langs moet. Je krijgt geen telefoon om acht uur ’s avonds.

Loop je bij een klant vast, dan bellen onze specialisten in en kijken ze met je mee. Die zitten bij ons in dienst, dus je hebt ze binnen een minuut aan de lijn. Geen half uur in de wacht bij een ketelmerk dat er geen belang bij heeft dat jouw storing vandaag opgelost wordt. Wij hebben hetzelfde doel als jij, dus die stap slaan we over.

Zit iemand in het weekend zonder warm water, dan schakelen wij een cv-monteur in en betalen dat zelf. Onze warmtepompboiler heeft bovendien een elektrisch element, dus niemand staat koud.

Je werkt zelfstandig vanuit je bus, maar je zit in een serviceteam en hebt korte lijnen met het magazijn en met productontwikkeling.

WAT DIT JE OPLEVERT

Over twee jaar ken jij deze systemen beter dan bijna iedereen in dit land, simpelweg omdat er nog maar weinig mensen zijn die er dagelijks aan werken. Dat is een positie die je zelf in handen hebt, en die alleen maar meer waard wordt.

Daar komt bij: omdat wij het product zelf maken, gaat wat jij in het veld ziet rechtstreeks naar de engineers. Je lost niet alleen storingen op, je zorgt dat ze de volgende keer niet meer voorkomen.

WAT JE MEEBRENGT

  • Een paar jaar ervaring als loodgieter, servicemonteur, storingsmonteur, installatiemonteur W, cv-monteur of monteur werktuigbouwkundige installaties

  • Of een technische mbo-opleiding met de praktijkervaring die daarbij hoort. Starters zoeken we niet

  • Ervaring met leidingwerk. Dat is het enige wat we niet in een paar maanden kunnen bijbrengen. De elektra kant en onze eigen warmtepompen leren we je wel

  • Rijbewijs B

  • Nederlands of Engels waarmee je een klant kunt uitleggen wat er aan de hand is

  • Zin om een nieuwe techniek onder de knie te krijgen

Bij de klant ben jij DeWarmte. Iemand moet blij zijn dat jij binnenkomt en het gevoel hebben: die gaat het voor mij oplossen. En omdat we hard groeien, is de situatie op locatie niet altijd zoals hij op je werkbon staat. Soms wil de klant er nog iets bij, soms is de voorbereiding niet compleet. Dan zoek jij een oplossing in plaats van een schuldige.

Twijfel je of je past? Bel of app Marvin even op 06 1111 9775.

We zoeken nu versterking in de driehoek Zwolle, Apeldoorn en Deventer. Woon je daar in de buurt, dan zetten we een voorraadpunt bij jou in de regio neer zodat je niet steeds naar Utrecht hoeft.

WAT JE KRIJGT

– € 3.000 tot € 5.000 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van je ervaring

– Een werkweek van 38 uur, of 40 uur met dertien ADV-dagen. Jij kiest

– Parttime kan ook, vanaf 24 uur per week

– 25 vakantiedagen bij fulltime, plus 8% vakantiegeld dat we maandelijks uitbetalen

– Een volledig uitgeruste bedrijfsbus, laptop en telefoon

– Reistijd is werktijd, vanaf het moment dat je instapt

– Opleidingen en trainingen tot je specialist bent in warmtepompen

– Deelname aan ons SAR-programma en mee op de jaarlijkse winterreis

MET WIE JE WERKT

Je komt in het serviceteam van Lars Steverink, Head of Service. Hij startte vijf jaar geleden bij DeWarmte toen het bedrijf uit vier mensen bestond en bouwde de serviceorganisatie op. Je werkt dagelijks samen met de servicecoördinatie in Den Haag die je route plant, met het magazijn in Utrecht en met de engineers die de warmtepompen ontwerpen.

HOE HET GAAT

We nemen op dit moment ongeveer vier mensen per maand aan, en de teams die we nu bouwen moeten staan voor de piek aan het eind van het jaar. Reageer je deze week, dan zit je er nog bij.

  1. Bel of app Marvin op 06 1111 9775, of stuur je cv. Een motivatiebrief hoeft niet.

Compensation: €3K – €5K per month

Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR

Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats.

France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa, the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.


The role

As Embedded System Lead Engineer, you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it.

What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget.

You will lead their technical development, from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come.

These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge, on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role.

The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it.

What you'll own

  • Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications.

  • The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt.

  • Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS).

  • The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment.

  • Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore.

  • Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench.

  • Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units.

The hard problems you'll be solving

These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point:

  • Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling.

  • Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell.

  • Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible.

  • Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it.

  • Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean.

Who we're looking for

You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically:

  • 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world.

  • Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems. This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space.

  • Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack: electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal.

  • Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control.

  • Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do.

  • A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters.

  • Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it.

Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale.

Why join now

  • Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that.

  • A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space.

  • Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years.

  • AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about.

  • A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it.

About Plane

Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together.

 

Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 55,000+ stars, 5,000+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship.

 

Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules.

 

Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work.

 

Humans and agents

We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's.

 

Most software treats AI as a feature. We treat agents as a kind of worker, and that changes what the system underneath has to be. Agents are only as good as the context they can see and the state they are allowed to change, so shared context, explicit state, durable history, and accountable action are not items on our roadmap. They are the product. Plane is built so that when an agent acts, the humans responsible can see what happened, why, and on whose authority, and the record survives.

 

This is what the infrastructure is for: making the future where humans and agents work together useful, legible, and fully within the organization's control. Every role at Plane is some part of building that.

 

About the role

Our largest customers do not buy Plane off the shelf. A bank wants it behind their firewall with SSO tied to their identity provider; a defense contractor wants it air-gapped with a migration plan from three legacy tools at once. You will own the technical architecture for these deployments before the contract is signed and after, translating what a customer's infrastructure and compliance team requires into a Plane deployment that actually holds up. You will work directly with sales on the largest deals we run and with engineering when a customer's requirements push past what we support today. This role exists because our regulated-industry customers ask questions our sales team cannot answer alone, and our engineers should not have to answer on every call.

 

What you'll do

  • Own the technical architecture for enterprise and regulated-industry deployments, from the first discovery call through a signed statement of work.

  • Design self-hosted and air-gapped Plane deployments that satisfy a specific customer's security review, not a generic best-practice checklist.

  • Run technical discovery with customers whose infrastructure and compliance teams will pick apart every answer you give, and be right often enough that they trust the next one.

  • Define the migration path when a customer moves off two or three existing tools at once, including what data does not survive the move and saying so up front.

  • Work daily with sales on live deals and with engineering when a customer's requirements expose a real gap in the product, carrying that gap back as a specific, scoped request rather than a vague one.

  • Answer the same security questionnaire in a slightly different format for the fourth time this month, because every regulated buyer's procurement process is its own small bureaucracy and none of them read each other's paperwork.

 

What you'll bring

  • You have designed and defended a technical architecture to a skeptical buyer, and you can walk us through one deal where the customer's own security or infrastructure team changed your design.

  • You understand self-hosted and on-premises deployment beyond a docker-compose file, including networking, SSO and identity federation, and what changes when a customer runs the software instead of you.

  • You can read a security questionnaire or compliance requirement and translate it into an actual deployment decision, not a reassurance.

  • You are comfortable being the technical voice on a sales call, including the parts where the answer is no or not yet.

  • You write technical documentation a customer's own engineers will actually follow, because you will not be in the room when they run it.

 

Nice to haves

  • You have worked pre-sales or post-sales in a solutions architecture, sales engineering, or technical account management role selling to regulated industries.

  • You have contributed to Plane, run it self-hosted, or maintained another open project people rely on.

  • You have shipped or supported deployments into banking, defense, healthcare, or air-gapped environments specifically.

  • You have opinions about how AI agents should be permissioned and audited in an enterprise environment, and can defend them.

 

Tech

  • Backend: Python/Django, Golang, Node.js, Postgres, Redis

  • Messaging: RabbitMQ, Kafka

  • Infrastructure: AWS, Kubernetes, Rancher, self-hosted deployment via Docker and Helm

  • Identity: SAML, OIDC, SCIM

  • Everyday tools: GitHub, Plane (yes, we run on it), Figma, Slack

Why Plane?

Every company says it is different. We will try evidence instead.

 

The scope is real. We are a passion team serving companies of every size, including some of the largest in the world. Something you ship this month will run inside a Fortune 500 company and a 50-person startup in the same week, and you will hear from both.

 

The constraints make you better. Plane runs in our cloud, in customers' clouds, and on machines that will never touch the internet. Much of the work happens in the open, where the issues, the fixes, and the roadmap conversations are public. Building software that survives all of that is harder than building an ordinary SaaS product, and it is a better education than most companies can offer.

 

The people-and-agents future is being built here, in production. We think humans and AI agents will share one system of action for work. We are building that system now, for customers who already depend on it, and you will work on that problem directly whatever your role.

 

Your name is on the work. The teams are deeply connected enough that credit and responsibility both find you fast. That is some pressure. Mostly it is the fun part.

If that sounds like your kind of place, we would like to meet you.

Akeneo is the leading AI-powered Product Data Platform that helps brands, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers unify product data and pricing to power better product experiences, smarter decisions, and business growth in an AI-driven commerce world.

We’re all about experience - from the best-in-class product we build to the inspiring environment we create for our employees. You’ll grow in a dynamic environment where your ideas and expertise will make an impact from day one. Our flexible work model empowers you to thrive, balancing professional success with personal fulfilment. At Akeneo, you’ll be part of a supportive and collaborative team that values open communication, shared successes, and meaningful relationships.

The Team and Areas of Ownership

The SDM team owns the Akeneo Supplier Data Manager, the front door to the Akeneo Product Cloud for data.

SDM is a painkiller, not a vitamin. Retailers and distributors don't adopt it because it's nice to have; they adopt it because, without it, onboarding supplier data is a manual, error-prone job that keeps products off the shelf. Hundreds of suppliers send product data in various formats (spreadsheets, PDFs, images), and that data must be cleaned, classified, enriched, and verified before it reaches the catalogue. SDM does this through a pipeline of connected modules: mapping, validation, classification, extraction, multi-destination distribution, and more.

The scale is what makes this hard. These are not small files you can hand to an LLM and get a clean answer back. Supplier catalogues are large, constantly changing, and full of industry-specific terms, formatting quirks, and domain knowledge that trip up general-purpose tools. Some of the processing is deterministic; some of it isn't. Building systems that handle all of it reliably, at volume, across hundreds of supplier configurations, is the engineering problem you'd be here to help solve.

SDM is a cross-functional team that owns its work end-to-end and prides itself on solving the right problems, not just shipping code. Leadership sets direction and decides how much to invest in each problem; we own how to get there. When priorities compete, we make the trade-off together, grounded in customer data rather than opinion, and we're comfortable saying no to work that doesn't move the needle. The team is in a period of real investment and acceleration, and we're hiring engineers to help own SDM's future.

We're hiring at multiple levels on this team. This is the Software Engineer role for people on the rise. If you already have deep experience, our Senior Software Engineer opening is likely the better fit; you can always change once you speak to us.

What You Will Deliver In The Role…

  • Ship features across SDM: build and ship real features end-to-end, across the data-processing back end and the TypeScript and React front end, with the team alongside you.
  • Work on the data-processing pipelines: the core of SDM turns messy supplier data into trusted, high-volume catalogue data. Some steps are deterministic; some use LLMs to extract attributes and classify products. You'll help make them reliable, and you'll learn how to handle real problems of scale and correctness as you go.
  • Own what you build: as you grow, you'll take on more end-to-end, from shipping to monitoring in production to closing the loop with support. A weekly support rotation is shared across the team.
  • Grow into a senior engineer: through code review, pairing, and a wider Staff Engineering group invested in helping you get there.
  • Take part in customer discovery: see how customers actually work, and how their feedback shapes what we build.
  • Work across the Product Cloud: collaborate with adjacent teams and learn how the wider platform fits together.


What Will Set You Up For Success At Akeneo…

You don't need to be a senior, and you don't need a specialist background or a big name on your CV. You need the makings of a strong engineer: real problem-solving instinct, curiosity, drive, and solid fundamentals to build on. This is a team working on genuinely hard problems, so being excited to learn here means being excited to learn things and to be stretched. You'll grow fast, with a senior team and a wider Staff Engineering group to learn from.

  • You think, not just code. You want to understand why something is being built and how it really works, not just close the ticket. When you hit something you don't know, you dig in rather than paper over it.
  • You're building strong fundamentals. You generally know your way around different data structures and algorithms, and you're learning to reason about system design. You care about writing code that works properly, not just code that looks like it works.
  • You want to go deep when things get hard. When something breaks or confuses you, you want the real cause, not just to make the error go away. You like debugging, experimenting, and getting to the bottom of things.
  • You're comfortable across the stack, or keen to be. SDM spans data-processing back ends and a TypeScript and React front end. You don't need to be expert at both, but you're happy moving between them and eager to broaden.
  • You know at least one of Python, PHP, or JavaScript and TypeScript, and you pick up new ones fast. Python powers our data pipelines; PHP underpins the wider Akeneo Product Cloud; TypeScript and React cover the front end. You'll use more than one over time, and learning quickly matters more than which you start with.
  • You care about the customer. You want to know who uses what you build and why it matters to them.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity, or want to get there. We won't hand you a detailed spec for everything. You'll get clear problems and the room to solve them, with support when you need it.
  • You use AI to think, not just to type. We build with tools like Claude Code. The point isn't to churn out more code; it's to use AI to explore, experiment, and reason through problems, and to learn faster. When anyone can generate code, the value is in knowing what to build and why. (This is about how we build, not what we build.)

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris.
